# pigorc — configuring pigo

pigo is configured by a **Bash script** (`pigorc`) plus an optional static
`config.toml`. Because a pigorc is real Bash, includes, conditionals, variables and
`$(command)` secret lookups all work.

**The authoritative, machine-generated reference lives next to this file as
`reference.md`.** It is rewritten from the running binary on every launch, so it
always lists exactly the options, provider/agent fields, hook events, environment
variables and CLI flags this build supports. Read it before answering detailed
questions; use this file for the workflow and the recipes.

## Where configuration lives

Lowest to highest precedence:

1. Built-in defaults.
2. `~/.config/pigo/config.toml` (static file; `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` honored).
3. `$PIGO_HOME/config.json` (global) and `./.pigo/config.json` (project, only in a
   trusted directory): `model`, `provider`, `thinkingLevel`, `credentials`,
   `hooks`.
4. **pigorc**: `$PIGO_HOME/pigorc` (default `~/.pigo/pigorc`, always loaded) and
   `./.pigorc` (only in a trusted directory). Both are sourced by one `bash`
   process, global first, so the project file can refine or cancel the global one.
5. CLI flags (always win).

pigorc `option` values outrank both config files; exported variables join the
environment (provider keys, `<PROVIDER>_BASE_URL`, `PIGO_*`). Hooks merge by event
across every layer, and the script's hooks run last.

## The DSL

```bash
# 1) options — any config.toml key (see reference.md for the full table)
option model "zai/glm-4.6"
option thinking-level high
option allowed-tools read          # list keys append
option allowed-tools grep
option reset allowed-tools         # clear a list
option memory.enabled false        # nested tables use dots
option checkpoint.push-caps.memory 900

# 2) hooks — command form (same wire contract as config.json hooks)
hook add PreToolUse --matcher '^bash$' --timeout 5 --command './.pigo/hooks/no-rm.sh'

# 3) hooks — shell-function form: the function name is the event
PreToolUse() {
  # stdin is one line of JSON; exit 0 allows, exit 2 blocks (stderr = reason)
  grep -q 'rm -rf /' <<<"$(cat)" && { echo 'dangerous command' >&2; exit 2; }
  return 0
}
post_tool_use() { gofmt -w . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; }   # 9 events, any spelling

# 4) third-party provider
provider add mycorp --type openai --base-url "https://llm.mycorp.com/v1" \
  --env-var MYCORP_API_KEY --model mycorp-large
provider remove mycorp

# 5) custom sub-agent (agents are defined in the pigorc only)
agent add researcher --description "Read-only researcher" \
  --prompt-file ~/.pigo/prompts/researcher.md \
  --tools read,grep,find --model claude-haiku-4 --thinking off --timeout 300
agent hook researcher PreToolUse --matcher '^bash$' --command './hooks/no-bash.sh'
agent remove researcher

# 6) environment — provider keys, base URLs, PIGO_* knobs
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="$(pass show anthropic)"
export PIGO_MAX_SUBAGENTS=4
```

The script runs with `set -eu`: a failing statement aborts the load (options
applied so far are kept) and prints a warning. A missing bash, a 15s timeout, an
unknown option key or a malformed value only warns — configuration never blocks
the launch.

## Recipes

**Switch the default model.** `option model "zai/glm-4.6"` (or a bare provider name
like `zai` to use that provider's default). `option thinking-level high` for
reasoning effort.

**Point at a self-hosted or third-party gateway.** Either
`provider add <name> --type openai|anthropic --base-url URL [--env-var VAR]
[--model id]...`, then `option provider <name>` and `option model <id>`; or for a
one-off, `option base-url …` + `option protocol …`. The key comes from the declared
env var (default `<NAME>_API_KEY`), a named credential, or an inline `--api-key`
(the environment still wins). Defined providers behave like built-ins: `/model`
switching, model-id inference and the preset picker all see them.

**Define a custom sub-agent.** `agent add …` registers a tool named after the
agent: its own system prompt, tool allow list, model, reasoning effort, timeout,
hooks and isolation. Sub-agents are complete agents — own context, own persisted
session (parented to the calling conversation, hidden from `/resume`), automatic
compaction — and they never get the `question` tool. When a child needs a decision
it says so in its report; ask the user yourself, then continue that child with the
`session_id` its result reported. Add `"background": true` to a call to run it in
the background: the report arrives as a follow-up message and `task_output` lists
or waits for jobs.

**MCP servers.** `mcp add <name> --command CMD [--arg A ...] [--env K V ...]` for a
stdio server, or `mcp add <name> --url URL [--header K V ...]` for an HTTP one
(Streamable HTTP by default; `--transport sse` for the legacy HTTP+SSE flavor;
`--oauth` when the endpoint requires authorization; `--timeout N` / `--disabled`
optional). Tools appear as `mcp__<name>__<tool>`; a server advertising resources or
prompts also gets `mcp__<name>__list_resources` / `read_resource` and
`list_prompts` / `get_prompt`. `--no-tools` disables MCP along with the other
tools, a server that fails to start is reported and skipped, and a
`tools/list_changed` notification refreshes the tool set on the next turn.

**Hooks.** Per agent, hooks are its own by default (`inherit_hooks` / `--inherit-hooks`
also runs the global/project set). Sub-agent runs end on `SubagentStop`, not `Stop`.
Hook input is one line of JSON on stdin; exit codes and stdout JSON follow the same
contract as config.json hooks (blocking events: `PreToolUse`, `UserPromptSubmit`,
`Stop`, `SubagentStop`).

**Memory, compaction, dream.** `option memory.enabled false`,
`option checkpoint.thresholds 50%` (repeatable),
`option checkpoint.reserved 8192` (or `10%`),
`option checkpoint.push-caps.memory 800`, `option compaction.max-context 300K`,
`option dream.enabled false`.

**Trust and secrets.** `option approve true` trusts the working directory for this
run. Keep secrets out of config files: export the provider key or use
`option credential <name>` with `$PIGO_HOME/.credentials.yaml` (mode 0600).

**Only on the command line.** `-p/--print`, `--cwd`, `--no-tui`, `--version`,
`--list-sessions`, `--resume`/`--continue`, `--subagent-rpc`, `--dream*`,
`--github-review*`, `--append-system-prompt`, `--prompt-template`,
`--no-prompt-templates` describe one invocation, not durable configuration.

## Verifying and troubleshooting

- `pigo --help` lists the flags; `reference.md` (this directory) lists everything,
  regenerated from the binary.
- Startup warnings name the offending key: `pigorc: unknown option "x"` /
  `option x: "v" is not a boolean` — fix and rerun.
- To trace the script: `bash -x ~/.pigo/pigorc 2>&1 | head`.
- A project `.pigorc` and project hooks load only when the directory is trusted
  (fail-closed); run `pigo --approve` once or trust it in the REPL/TUI.
- Edits take effect without a restart in the interactive modes: the config files
  are re-read when they change before the next turn, and `/reload` applies them
  immediately. A reload keeps the session's own state (background jobs, todo list,
  scheduled reminders, background sub-agents, memory store, plugin processes) and
  leaves the previous configuration running if the new one cannot be assembled.
- Call the built-in `pigo_config` tool (or ask the agent to) to see what is actually
  in effect in this run: the config files that were read versus skipped, the
  resolved model/endpoint/thinking level, the tools and the boundary, skills, MCP
  servers with their connection state, the resolved hooks, sub-agents and memory
  settings. Pass `{"section": "hooks"}` (or `files`, `tools`, `skills`, `mcp`,
  `agents`, `memory`, `runtime`) to narrow it.

## Safety

pigorc is trusted code: it executes with your privileges before the UI appears, and
hook commands do too. Only point it at files you control, and keep the project file
in a trusted repository.
